comparisons.peer_summary: AMD continued investing in the open ROCm software stack, making key optimizations and adding features in the latest release to improve performance for generative AI workloads and simplify the developer experience.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD explicitly disclose the use of AI or machine learning technologies to enhance the performance and capabilities of their computing platforms. AVGO describes VeloRAIN using AI/ML to improve distributed workload security and performance, while AMD details investments in its ROCm software stack to optimize AI training and inference workloads, noting specific performance increases in generative AI. Both companies frame AI/ML not just as a product feature but as a core technology driver for their respective data center and infrastructure solutions.

sentences.text: • VeloRAIN: Our architecture uses AI or machine learning to improve the performance and security of distributed workloads.

We continued to invest in driving software capabilities and the open ecosystem to deliver powerful new features and capabilities in the AMD ROCm™ open software stack, bringing the latest features to highly-performant AI training and inference on AMD platforms.

During the year, we made several key optimizations and additional features in the latest AMD ROCm software that increases performance in key generative AI workloads, adds expanded support and optimization for additional frameworks and libraries, and simplifies the overall developer experience.

comparisons.peer_topic: Software strategy and open source contributions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel aims to optimize AI frameworks and maintains the OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference. In 2024, Intel launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation and contributed oneAPI specifications to the UXL Foundation to enable open, multi-vendor programming across accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and INTC both highlight strategic investments in software and AI frameworks to drive product competitiveness and user experience. AVGO's VeloRAIN uses AI to improve distributed workload performance, aligning with INTC's strategy to optimize AI frameworks (like PyTorch, TensorFlow) and its OpenVINO toolkit to efficiently run AI workloads on its hardware. Both disclosures emphasize that software and AI algorithms are critical to unlocking the potential of their underlying silicon and infrastructure.

sentences.text: • VeloRAIN: Our architecture uses AI or machine learning to improve the performance and security of distributed workloads.
We aim to optimize AI frameworks and middleware, such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, vLLM, Hugging Face and WebNN to run efficiently on our hardware.

Our OpenVINO™ toolkit is an open source toolkit that accelerates deep learning inference on our processors across various use cases, such as generative AI, computer vision, audio, and language with industry standard models.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, the company began shipping Micron G9 TLC based NAND in SSDs designed for low-latency, high-throughput workloads including AI training, machine learning, and cloud computing.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU identify AI training and machine learning as key high-performance workloads driving demand for their technologies. AVGO addresses these needs by using AI/ML within its VeloRAIN architecture to secure and optimize distributed workloads, whereas MU focuses on the underlying storage infrastructure, shipping G9 TLC NAND SSDs designed to meet the low-latency and high-throughput requirements of AI training and machine learning data-centric workloads.

sentences.text: • VeloRAIN: Our architecture uses AI or machine learning to improve the performance and security of distributed workloads.

In 2024, we also began shipping Micron G9 TLC based NAND in SSDs designed to deliver the transfer rates required to meet the low-latency and high-throughput needs of data-centric workloads from AI training and machine learning to unstructured databases, self-driving cars, and cloud computing.

comparisons.peer_summary: GPU parallel processing capabilities are essential for deep learning, enabling AI solutions like generative AI and recommendation systems to deliver services difficult or impossible with traditional coding.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and NVDA both describe the application of AI and machine learning as central to their value proposition in generating content and enabling complex computing tasks. AVGO's VeloRAIN uses ML to improve distributed workload performance, while NVDA explains that GPU parallel processing is essential for deep learning algorithms that serve as the 'brain' for AI solutions like generative AI. Both companies position AI/ML not merely as an add-on but as a fundamental architectural component enabling advanced services.

sentences.text: • VeloRAIN: Our architecture uses AI or machine learning to improve the performance and security of distributed workloads.
Its parallel processing capabilities, supported by thousands of computing cores, are essential for deep learning algorithms.
GPU-powered AI solutions are being developed by thousands of enterprises to deliver services and products that would have been immensely difficult or even impossible with traditional coding.

Examples include generative AI, which can create new content such as text, code, images, audio, video, and molecule structures, and recommendation systems, which can recommend highly relevant content such as products, services, media or ads using deep neural networks trained on vast datasets that capture the user preferences.

comparisons.peer_topic: Intellectual property portfolio and technology scope
comparisons.peer_summary: The company owns significant IP in CDMA/OFDMA technologies and develops other key technologies including video/audio codecs, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, AI, machine learning, and RF/RFFE designs, some of which become industry standards.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and QCOM list AI and machine learning as key technologies within their broader intellectual property and product portfolios. AVGO specifically mentions VeloRAIN's use of AI/ML to improve distributed workloads, while QCOM identifies AI and machine learning techniques as core technologies developed and commercialized alongside other mobile and wireless standards. Both firms treat AI/ML as a critical component of their technology scope and innovation strategy.

sentences.text: • VeloRAIN: Our architecture uses AI or machine learning to improve the performance and security of distributed workloads.

We have also developed other technologies that are used by wireless and other devices that are not related to industry standards, such as operating systems, user interfaces, graphics and camera processing functionality, RF (radio frequency), RFFE (radio frequency front-end) and antenna designs, AI and machine learning techniques and application processor architectures, among other technologies.
